parts.note: Your tailnet keeps it private, and plain HTTP is fine there. HTTPS (Tailscale Serve) is optional.

guides.why: Agents run on machines; the hub's own machine can be one.

values.value: Paste it on Administration › Claude, with an endpoint if you use a gateway; the app seals it on your device.

parts.note: The invite is a link and a code, for one person, good for 7 days. Send it to them yourself.
parts.title: Invite someone

guides.title: Invite people
guides.why: Each person gets their own sign-in, chats and Navi; you choose who is an admin.

guides.fieldsNote: Save the client ID and secret, and the Gmail subscription and key if you set them up, on Administration › Google: the app seals the secrets on your device. Then each person connects their own Google account from their Navi; if a sign-in lapses, Navi offers Reconnect.

values.label: Project name
values.note: Keep the project ID the same as the name. IDs are global across Google Cloud: if fleetd-devbox is taken, take the ID Google offers and use it wherever fleetd-devbox appears below.

parts.title: Turn on Gmail, Calendar and Drive

values.label: Audience
values.value: Internal if everyone is in your Google Workspace; otherwise External.

values.label: Publishing status
values.value: External: press Publish app, so it is In production. In Testing, Google ends each connection after 7 days.

parts.note: Gmail and Drive are restricted scopes: until Google verifies the app, people see a warning when they connect and press Advanced, then Go to the app. An unverified app takes up to 100 people.
parts.title: Add the scopes

values.label: Draft and send
values.note: Drafts, sends and replies. It can't delete mail or change labels.

values.label: Drive
values.note: Searching, reading, uploading and sharing files.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.note: Nothing to register: a Desktop app client takes it on any port. When someone connects, the fleetd app listens on a free port on their own computer, and Google sends them back there.

parts.note: New mail reaches Navi in seconds. Gmail publishes to a Pub/Sub topic and fleetd pulls from it, so no public address is needed. Without it, Navi checks Gmail about every minute.
parts.title: Gmail in real time

values.label: Topic ID
values.note: Untick "Add a default subscription". Its full name is projects/fleetd-devbox/topics/fleetd-gmail.

values.label: Publisher on the topic
values.note: Topic › Permissions › Add principal, role Pub/Sub Publisher. Gmail publishes as this account.

values.label: Subscription ID
values.note: Topic fleetd-gmail, delivery type Pull. Its full name is projects/fleetd-devbox/subscriptions/fleetd-gmail-hub.

parts.note: A service account that may only read the subscription. Its key goes to one machine, which pulls new-mail notices and passes them to the hub.
parts.title: A key to read it

values.label: Service account ID
values.note: No project roles: skip the optional steps and press Done.

values.label: Subscriber on the subscription
values.note: Subscriptions › the subscription above › Permissions › Add principal, role Pub/Sub Subscriber.

values.label: Key
values.value: Service accounts › the account above › Keys › Add key › Create new key › JSON. Paste the downloaded file on Administration › Google, then delete it.

values.label: Or in Cloud Shell
values.note: Both parts in one go, in project fleetd-devbox: it prints the key once, to paste. A new account can take a minute to show up; if the Subscriber grant says it doesn't exist, run the last three lines again. If your organization refuses the key (iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation), an organization admin lifts that policy for this project; or leave real-time mail off, and Navi checks mail about every minute.
values.value:
gcloud config set project fleetd-devbox
SA=fleetd-gmail-reader@fleetd-devbox.iam.gserviceaccount.com
gcloud services enable pubsub.googleapis.com &&
gcloud pubsub topics create fleetd-gmail &&
gcloud pubsub topics add-iam-policy-binding fleetd-gmail --member=serviceAccount:gmail-api-push@system.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/pubsub.publisher &&
gcloud pubsub subscriptions create fleetd-gmail-hub --topic=fleetd-gmail &&
gcloud iam service-accounts create fleetd-gmail-reader &&
sleep 30 &&
gcloud pubsub subscriptions add-iam-policy-binding fleetd-gmail-hub --member=serviceAccount:$SA --role=roles/pubsub.subscriber &&
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create key.json --iam-account=$SA &&
cat key.json && rm key.json

guides.test: Ask Google whether it knows this client
guides.title: Google
guides.why: Each person's Navi reads and drafts their mail, calendar and Drive, through a Google client you own.

parts.note: Nothing to set up for the hub: each person connects Notion on their Navi's Integrations, with an internal integration of their own, and shares with it only the pages Navi may use.
